questions.prompt: What creates a durable sense of meaning or purpose?
What sustains motivation once the initial drive fades?

vocabularyClusters.definition: Meaning/purpose is produced by a deliberate inner practice, not received passively.

termsByBook.termAsUsed: the three roads to meaning (work, love, suffering)

vocabularyClusters.definition: A repeated, deliberate inner practice (not a one-time insight) is what keeps motivation or meaning alive over time.

positions.stance: Meaning is forged retroactively, through how one responds to unchosen suffering (tragic optimism).
Meaning/purpose is built proactively, through preparation and eliminating doubt before adversity arrives.

conflictClusters.topic: Where does lasting motivation come from once initial resolve fades?

positions.stance: Motivation is sustained by an existential will oriented toward a specific meaning, not by willpower alone.
Motivation is sustained by meditation that produces inner peace and harmony, which in turn removes doubt.
Motivation is sustained mechanically through a three-pillar loop: mind conditioning feeds meditation, which feeds repeated action, which reinforces the mind.

crossEdges.label: both frame meaning as a discipline, not a discovery
both use meditation as the practice that removes doubt and stabilizes drive
both locate the root of motivation in an oriented inner will/mind, not external reward
